questions.question: You should cover cargo to:

options.text: Protect it from thieves.
Protect it from weather.
Keep other drivers from seeing what is inside.
Keep it secret.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect it from weather.
questions.explanation: Cover cargo to protect it from weather and to prevent it from spilling on other drivers.

questions.question: What does the air compressor governor do?

options.text: Controls when the air compressor pumps air into the air storage tanks.
Controls how fast air leaves the air storage tanks.
Controls the temperature of air going into the air storage tanks.
Controls the temperature of air leaving the air storage tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Controls when the air compressor pumps air into the air storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor controls when air is pumped into the air storage tanks.

questions.question: The drive shaft should:

options.text: Be bent toward the passenger side.
Be bent toward the driver's side.
Be bent to one side.
Not be bent.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not be bent.
questions.explanation: During a vehicle inspection, check that the drive shaft is not bent or cracked.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air brake system, you must wait for the air compressor to build a minimum of ____ in both the primary and secondary systems.

options.text: 25 psi
50 psi
75 psi
100 psi

questions.correctAnswerText: 100 psi
questions.explanation: Before driving a dual air brake system, wait for the air compressor to build at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems.

questions.question: When a brake pedal is pressed and the S-cam turns, the S-cam:

options.text: Presses the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum.
Tightens the brake drum onto the axle.
Presses the brake lining against the wheel.
Releases air from the air tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Presses the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum.
questions.explanation: When the brake pedal is pressed, the S-cam turns and presses the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum. This creates friction and slows the vehicle.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: Allow the rear wheels to lock up.
Allow all wheels to lock up.
Prevent wheel lockup.
Alert other drivers when you are braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent wheel lockup.
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents wheels from locking up when you brake hard on a slippery surface.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver confronts you, you should not:

options.text: Challenge them.
Ignore their gestures.
Avoid making eye contact.
Try to get out of their way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Challenge them.
questions.explanation: When facing an aggressive driver, get out of their way. Do not make eye contact, race, or stay in their path. Ignore any gestures meant to provoke you.

questions.question: When driving, it is important to:

options.text: Keep your attention focused in front.
Look only in front and to the right.
Look only in front and to the sides.
Look to the front, sides, and rear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look to the front, sides, and rear.
questions.explanation: Safe driving requires awareness of all sides of your vehicle. Check your mirrors often to see what is ahead, to the sides, and to the rear.

questions.question: If you are convicted of a traffic violation in your personal car:

options.text: The officer will tell your employer.
Your CDL is not affected because the violation is on your personal license.
You should tell your employer within six months.
You must tell your employer within 30 days.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must tell your employer within 30 days.
questions.explanation: You must tell your employer within 30 days of any traffic violation conviction, no matter which vehicle you were driving. Parking violations do not need to be reported.

questions.question: If your vehicle is hydroplaning, you should:

options.text: Speed up.
Not apply the brakes.
Put the vehicle in reverse.
Turn the steering wheel hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not apply the brakes.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle hydroplanes, do not use the brakes. Release the accelerator and push in the clutch to slow down and regain traction.

questions.question: A driver should always:

options.text: Stay in the right lane.
Have a plan for emergencies.
Stay in the left lane.
Drive above the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have a plan for emergencies.
questions.explanation: Watch the road ahead to spot hazards early. Plan how you will handle dangerous situations before they happen.

questions.question: If exiting a bus during the basic vehicle control skills test, you must:

options.text: Keep both hands on the handrail.
Not touch the handrail.
Hold the handrail firmly at all times.
Rush down the stairs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handrail firmly at all times.
questions.explanation: When exiting your vehicle during the basic vehicle control skills test, face the vehicle and keep three points of contact at all times. For a bus, you must hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly can cause you to fail the test.

questions.question: Always drive so your vehicle can stop:

options.text: Within 10 feet of where you are now.
Within 1,000 feet of where you are now.
Within the distance you can see ahead.
Immediately.

questions.correctAnswerText: Within the distance you can see ahead.
questions.explanation: Drive at a speed that allows you to stop completely within the area of road you can see in front of you.

questions.question: What is the best way to check your lights during a pre-trip inspection?

options.text: Park near a mirror and look for a reflection.
Turn on the lights, then get out and look at them.
Check the instrument panel for warning lights.
Drive in traffic and wait for other drivers to signal if lights are out.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on the lights, then get out and look at them.
questions.explanation: During a pre-trip inspection, turn on your lights and then exit the vehicle to look at them.

questions.question: Sending text messages while driving:

options.text: Is okay if the messages are short.
Is encouraged.
Is allowed if you are texting your employer.
Is not allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is not allowed.
questions.explanation: You cannot send or read text messages while driving.

questions.question: Blocking a load:

options.text: Is dangerous and should never be done.
Helps keep the load from shifting.
Is only done with liquids.
Can only be done in dry weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps keep the load from shifting.
questions.explanation: Blocking cargo prevents it from sliding during transport. Shifting cargo can make it harder to steer and control your vehicle.

questions.question: What is black ice?

options.text: A thick layer of ice on the road.
A thin layer of ice on the road.
Ice that is black from dirt on the road.
Ice that is easy to see.

questions.correctAnswerText: A thin layer of ice on the road.
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice. You can see the road surface through it. A road with black ice may just look wet.

questions.question: Move over laws require:

options.text: Trucks to use the left lane.
All vehicles to leave the lane next to a stopped emergency vehicle with its lights on.
All vehicles to use the left lane.
All vehicles to move to the left lane if a flatbed trailer is in the right lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: All vehicles to leave the lane next to a stopped emergency vehicle with its lights on.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle is stopped on the side of the road with its lights flashing, move to another lane if you can do so safely. If you cannot move over, slow down and drive carefully.

questions.question: When parked on the side of the road, you should:

options.text: Use only the rear flashing lights.
Use one set of turn signals.
Use your high beam headlights.
Use your four-way flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your four-way flashers.
questions.explanation: Turn on your four-way emergency flashers whenever you park on the side of the road. This is especially important at night.

questions.question: How many hours of sleep per night does an adult need to stay alert?

options.text: Six to seven hours
Seven to eight hours
Eight to nine hours

questions.correctAnswerText: Seven to eight hours
questions.explanation: Getting enough rest is important for safe driving. Most adults need seven to eight hours of sleep each night to stay alert.

questions.question: After you stop during the stop/start maneuver, you should:

options.text: Turn on the four-way flashers.
Not use the four-way flashers because this is a test, not an emergency.
Leave the vehicle in first gear.
Park in front of a fire hydrant.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on the four-way flashers.
questions.explanation: When you stop during the stop/start maneuver on the driving test, turn on your four-way flashers and shift into neutral or park. Do not block driveways, intersections, fire hydrants, or signs.

questions.question: After changing a tire, you should stop a short distance later to:

options.text: Check that the lug nuts are tight.
Make sure the tire tread is deep enough.
Confirm the correct tire was changed.
Check if rocks are stuck in the tread.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that the lug nuts are tight.
questions.explanation: After you change a tire, stop a short time later to check the lug nuts are tight.

questions.question: Texting while driving a commercial motor vehicle is:

options.text: Okay if the text is work-related.
Okay if the message has fewer than 10 words.
Encouraged because it is safer than talking on the phone.
Not allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not allowed.
questions.explanation: Texting while driving a commercial motor vehicle is illegal and dangerous. This includes typing text into or reading text from any electronic device.

questions.question: While driving, you should take a break ____ to prevent fatigue.

options.text: Every 30 minutes
Every hour
Every two hours
Every six hours

questions.correctAnswerText: Every two hours
questions.explanation: On a long trip, take a break at least once every two hours or every 100 miles to avoid becoming tired.

questions.question: One way to deal with blind spots is to:

options.text: Drive faster than other vehicles so they cannot pass you.
Drive in the left lane so you only need to watch vehicles on your right.
Check your mirrors often and know where nearby vehicles are.
Avoid using your mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors often and know where nearby vehicles are.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often to watch the traffic around you. This helps you notice when other vehicles move into your blind spots.

questions.question: What color is the low air pressure warning light?

options.text: Green
Orange
Red
Purple

questions.correctAnswerText: Red
questions.explanation: Vehicles with air brakes have a low air pressure warning light that is red. It may also have a buzzer sound.

questions.question: The application pressure gauge shows:

options.text: How much air pressure is applied to the brakes.
The temperature of air in the braking system.
The pressure of air coming from the compressor.
How many times the brakes have been used.

questions.correctAnswerText: How much air pressure is applied to the brakes.
questions.explanation: In an air brake system, the application pressure gauge shows how much air pressure is being applied to the brakes. Not all vehicles have this gauge.

questions.question: For winter driving, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: Front tires need a tread depth of at least 4/32 inch.
Tires should be slightly deflated.
Rear tires need a tread depth of at least 2/32 inch.
Use a gauge to check tread depth on each tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tires should be slightly deflated.
questions.explanation: In winter, your tires need good tread. Front tires need at least 4/32 inch tread in the main grooves, and rear tires need at least 2/32 inch. Use a gauge to check tread depth.

questions.question: Air tank drains are used to:

options.text: Let rainwater enter the tank.
Remove water and compressor oil from the air tank.
Never be opened.
Stay open while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove water and compressor oil from the air tank.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks in an air brake system need to be drained to remove water and compressor oil that builds up. Not draining them can cause damage. Drains should be opened at the end of each day of driving.

questions.question: If you stay in neutral too long while double clutching and cannot shift into the next gear, you should:

options.text: Stop the vehicle and start over.
Return to neutral, release the clutch, speed up, and try again.
Skip the gear you want and go into the next one.
Keep the vehicle in neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Return to neutral, release the clutch, speed up, and try again.
questions.explanation: If you stay in neutral too long while double clutching and have trouble shifting, do not force it. Return to neutral, release the clutch, increase engine speed to match road speed, and try again.

questions.question: How can you warn drivers behind you that you plan to slow down?

options.text: Press hard on the brakes all at once.
Tap the brakes a few times before slowing down.
Turn on one set of turn signals.
Put your hand out the driver's window and wave.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tap the brakes a few times before slowing down.
questions.explanation: Lightly tap your brake pedal a few times before you slow down. This flashes your brake lights and warns drivers behind you that you are about to slow down.

questions.question: When you stop, how should you press the brake pedal?

options.text: Press it down quickly.
Press it down gradually.
Lift it up quickly.
Lift it up gradually.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press it down gradually.
questions.explanation: Press the brake pedal down gradually when stopping. Use steady pressure so your vehicle stops slowly and safely.

questions.question: What is the number one cause of death and injury in work zones?

options.text: Speeding drivers
Careless behavior by construction workers
Drivers driving too slowly
Equipment in the roadway

questions.correctAnswerText: Speeding drivers
questions.explanation: Speeding is the main cause of death and injury in work zones. Drive carefully and slowly when you see road workers.

questions.question: What is sleep debt?

options.text: When you do not get enough sleep
When you want to take a nap
Getting too much sleep
The time it takes to get ready to drive after sleeping

questions.correctAnswerText: When you do not get enough sleep
questions.explanation: Sleep debt happens when you do not sleep enough. You can only pay back this debt by getting more sleep.

questions.question: Which of the following can stop someone from getting a hazardous materials endorsement?

options.text: They are not a lawful permanent resident of the United States.
They got a speeding ticket in the last three years.
They did not get every question right on the test.
They did not pass the test on the first try.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are not a lawful permanent resident of the United States.
questions.explanation: You will be denied a hazardous materials endorsement if you give up your U.S. citizenship, are not a lawful permanent resident, are wanted for or convicted of certain crimes, are judged mentally unfit, or the Transportation Security Administration (TSA) says you are a security risk.

questions.question: How should you do a pre-trip inspection?

options.text: In a different way each time.
In the same order every time.
Only when it is sunny.
Not at all if the vehicle seems to be running well.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the same order every time.
questions.explanation: Do your pre-trip inspection the same way before every drive. Using the same order helps you remember all the steps and makes sure you do not miss anything.

questions.question: What two things tell you when to shift to a higher gear?

options.text: Engine speed and road speed.
Other trucks and road conditions.
Timing and road position.
Oil pressure and air brake pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Engine speed and road speed.
questions.explanation: Two things tell you when to shift up. First is engine speed (rpm). Check your vehicle's manual for the correct rpm range and shift up when you reach the top. Second is road speed (mph). Learn which speeds work for each gear, then watch your speedometer and shift up as needed.

questions.question: How should cargo on flatbed trailers be secured?

options.text: Tied down.
Glued down.
Left loose.
Pushed to one side.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tied down.
questions.explanation: Cargo on flatbed trailers must be tied down to keep it from moving or falling during transport.

questions.question: What is a Gross Vehicle Weight Rating?

options.text: The maximum weight a fully loaded vehicle can weigh according to the manufacturer.
The maximum weight one vehicle can pull.
The minimum weight a vehicle must haul.
The maximum weight that can be loaded on a trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum weight a fully loaded vehicle can weigh according to the manufacturer.
questions.explanation: Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) is the maximum weight the manufacturer says a vehicle and its load can weigh.

questions.question: Which item is NOT required on a commercial vehicle?

options.text: A fire extinguisher.
Spare electrical fuses.
Warning devices for parked vehicles, such as flares.
A spotlight.

questions.correctAnswerText: A spotlight.
questions.explanation: Commercial vehicles must carry at least one fire extinguisher, spare electrical fuses (unless the vehicle has circuit breakers), and warning devices for parked vehicles such as warning triangles, flares, or liquid burning flares. A spotlight is not required.

questions.question: What type of force must emergency brakes use?

options.text: Air pressure
Mechanical
Heavy
Electrical

questions.correctAnswerText: Mechanical
questions.explanation: Air pressure can leak away over time. Emergency brakes in air brake systems must use mechanical force to stay engaged.

questions.question: How can you check if a trailer has ABS?

options.text: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors attached to the back of the brakes.
Look under the hood for the ABS sticker.
Look at the tires.
Remove a tire and look for the ABS sensor on the axle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors attached to the back of the brakes.
questions.explanation: To check if a trailer has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), look under the vehicle for the electronic control unit and wheel speed sensor wires at the back of the brakes.

questions.question: What should you do when using the controlled braking method in an emergency?

options.text: Press the brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels.
Press the brakes with about half your normal force.
Press the brakes so the wheels lock.
Press the brakes with minimal pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels.
questions.explanation: In an emergency stop, use controlled braking by pressing the brakes as hard as you can without locking the wheels. Keep your steering wheel movements small while braking.

questions.question: What happens when there is too little weight on the steering axle?

options.text: Poor traction.
Increased visibility.
Longer stopping distances.
Improved gas mileage.

questions.correctAnswerText: Poor traction.
questions.explanation: Cargo weight must be balanced properly for safe handling. If cargo is too far back, the front axle loses weight and the front wheels may not grip the road well enough for safe steering.

questions.question: What do air tank drains do?

options.text: Allow rain water to enter the tanks.
Remove water and oil from the tanks.
Should never be opened.
Must stay open while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove water and oil from the tanks.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks have drains to remove water and compressor oil. Water and oil left in the system can damage the brakes.

questions.question: What is true about pull-ups during the basic vehicle control skills test?

options.text: A pull-up always counts against the applicant.
You should do at least one pull-up.
Stopping without changing direction does not count as a pull-up.
Too many pull-ups are acceptable according to some test administrators.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stopping without changing direction does not count as a pull-up.
questions.explanation: A pull-up happens when you stop and pull forward to gain a better position. Stopping without moving forward does not count as a pull-up. Too many pull-ups will be marked as errors.

questions.question: If your vehicle stops on the road or shoulder, what must you do within 10 minutes?

options.text: Place emergency warning devices.
Alert local law enforcement.
Stand behind your vehicle and wave traffic around you.
Call a mechanic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Place emergency warning devices.
questions.explanation: You must place emergency warning devices, such as reflective warning triangles, within 10 minutes of stopping on the side of the road.

questions.question: During a vehicle inspection, lug nuts must be all of the following except:

options.text: Free of cracks.
Free of distortions.
Loose.
Free of rust.

questions.correctAnswerText: Loose.
questions.explanation: During a vehicle inspection, all lug nuts must be present, free of cracks and distortions, and tight with no signs of looseness like rust trails or shiny threads. All bolt holes must also be free of cracks and distortions.

questions.question: After changing a tire, why should you stop after a short distance?

options.text: To check that the wheel nuts are tight.
To check that the tire has enough air pressure.
To confirm the correct tire was changed.
To check that changing one tire did not damage another tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: To check that the wheel nuts are tight.
questions.explanation: After changing a tire, stop after a short distance to check that the wheel nuts are tight.

questions.question: During a vehicle inspection, you must demonstrate all of the following except:

options.text: That the oil pressure gauge is working.
That the oil pressure warning light turns off or the gauge shows normal pressure.
That the oil temperature gauge, if the vehicle has one, rises to normal operating temperature.
That the oil pressure gauge comes on when you use the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: That the oil pressure gauge comes on when you use the brakes.
questions.explanation: When checking the oil pressure gauge during a vehicle inspection, make sure it works and shows normal pressure or the warning light turns off. If the vehicle has an oil temperature gauge, it should gradually rise to normal operating temperature. The oil pressure gauge should not come on when you use the brakes.
